subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery policy should OpenClaw apply when an active session transcript is too large or dangerous to open during gateway restart?
rationale: The remaining fix may preserve, truncate, quarantine, skip, reset, or migrate user transcripts, and that choice affects recovery behavior, user data preservation, and unattended service availability.

options.title: Quarantine and degrade by default
options.body: Skip the oversized active transcript on startup, preserve it for doctor/manual recovery, and let the gateway continue without re-entering the crash loop.

options.title: Truncate oldest history automatically
options.body: Keep the session usable by rewriting to a bounded tail, but accept automatic loss of older transcript context.

options.title: Require manual operator repair
options.body: Fail with a clear doctor command and no automatic rewrite, preserving data but leaving unattended services down until action is taken.

recommendation.title: Quarantine and degrade by default
recommendation.body: Skip the oversized active transcript on startup, preserve it for doctor/manual recovery, and let the gateway continue without re-entering the crash loop.

likelyOwner.reason: The local snapshot and major refactor history point to this owner for the current runner/session architecture decision.
